name: Growing Teratoma Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Logothetis Criteria for Growing Teratoma Syndrome

criteria.description: History of nonseminomatous germ cell tumor treated with chemotherapy
Increase in tumor size or new tumor masses during or after chemotherapy despite normalized tumor markers
Histological confirmation of mature teratoma without malignant elements in resected masses
Serum tumor markers (AFP, β-hCG) normalized or decreased despite tumor growth

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria: prior germ cell tumor treated with chemotherapy, tumor growth during or after chemotherapy with normalized tumor markers, and histopathological confirmation of mature teratoma.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of viable malignant germ cell tumor components.

laboratory: Normalized serum tumor markers (AFP, β-hCG) despite tumor growth
imaging: Enlarging masses on CT or MRI in retroperitoneal, pelvic, or thoracic regions
Absence of new metastatic lesions typical for malignant germ cell tumors
other: Histopathology showing mature teratoma without malignant germ cell tumor components

distinguishingFeatures: Histopathology showing viable malignant germ cell tumor elements
Tumor growth associated with rising tumor markers
Tumor growth without histological evidence of mature teratoma

redFlags: Rapid enlargement of tumor masses despite normalized tumor markers
Development of new symptoms related to mass effect (e.g., urinary obstruction, bowel obstruction)
Histological evidence of malignant transformation within teratoma
